messages:
maya: quick check — we're preparing to enable fast_tokenizer_v2 for one enterprise customer (ACME, contract ACME-2025-PRO). Do we treat this as a per-customer allowlist flag or as contract-gated entitlement? I want a safe canary plan, kill-switch, and clear ops playbook. :eyes:

liam: +1 on per-customer flag but wired to contract gating. i.e., create flag fast_tokenizer_v2; default off; flag metadata includes contract_id so UI/infra can surface it. advantages: easy rollback, scoped rollout, and simpler telemetry.

sara: security checklist: confirm no new key material required. if we ship model shards or tokenization code to customer infra (private), we need KMS entry. For hosted/dedicated it's fine. Also add audit log entries for flag toggles.

ryan: product note — acme legal wants explicit opt-in window and a 24h notification before full enable. canary must start at account-level 0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with manual gates.

liam: proposed ops plan (short):
1) create flag: fast_tokenizer_v2 (scoped: org)
2) allowlist ACME org id: org_0xACME
3) canary slices: 5% account-ramp, monitor latency/error/failure-rate; abort if tokenization error > 0.5% or 95th latency regresses > 30ms
4) rollout script w/ built-in kill-switch and blast radius limiter

liam: example commands we'll use:```bash
# create flag in feature-store
redwood-ctl flags create fast_tokenizer_v2 --scope=org --default=off --meta='contract:ACME-2025-PRO'
# enable for org allowlist (canary)
redwood-ctl flags set --flag=fast_tokenizer_v2 --org=org_0xACME --on --slice=canary-5pct
# kill switch
redwood-ctl flags set --flag=fast_tokenizer_v2 --org=org_0xACME --off
```

engbot: note: automated smoke checks will run after any flag change. Please include CL link in toggle PR so infra can correlate. :robot_face:

ryan: pinging @eng-reviews — can someone take a quick look at the flag config PR when it's ready? small change but want to ensure the contract gating metadata is added.

liam: i'll open the PR in ~10m. PR will include: flag schema changes, audit logging hook, and one e2e test that flips flag for simulated org and validates tokenization fallback.

maya: thanks — ops question: how do we limit accidental broad enablement? need guardrails in console + API rate limits for flag writes.

liam: plan: server-side validation prevents enabling org-scoped flags without contract metadata and two-step confirmation in console for enterprise orgs. API will reject one-off global toggles for flags with contract meta.

ops-bot: scheduled action: canary ramp to 5% for org_0xACME in 30m unless block comment is added to the PR.

sara: quick checklist items for myself: add flag toggle to audit dashboards, hook KMS access review if private, and confirm retention of logs 90d for enterprise.

maya: perfect. i'll add a short line in the ACME runbook and update the customer-facing enablement doc — will reference the kill-switch CLI.

ryan: small ask: include a telemetry tag so we can slice traces by flag=fast_tokenizer_v2 and org=org_0xACME. that makes post-rollout analysis easier.

liam: yep will add telemetry tag + a fallback metric. also adding automatic rollback policy to the rollout job: if tokenization_error_rate > 0.5% for 3 consecutive minutes -> auto-off and notify #incidents.

maya: thanks all. if nobody objects i'll merge PR after one reviewer and kick off the canary later today. :white_check_mark:
